description: During pump maintenance, the technician removed the coupling guard and began work while the motor was still connected to the electrical supply.
Several unused cardboard boxes were left beside the entrance to the administration office.
A contractor opened a process drain line after assuming it had been isolated, but the line released a small amount of pressurized fluid.
The emergency shower near the laboratory had accumulated dust and required routine cleaning.
A worker was guiding a suspended pipe spool by hand while another worker stood on the opposite side of the load path.
The control room operator noticed that a corridor light was flickering and reported it for maintenance.
A technician entered a vessel to inspect an internal component after the previous shift had completed the gas test several hours earlier.
A visitor was not wearing the required identification badge and was stopped at the security gate.
During welding near a hydrocarbon process line, the team continued work after the atmospheric monitoring equipment stopped functioning.
A small amount of rainwater collected near the pedestrian walkway and was cleaned by the housekeeping team.
A worker was repairing equipment from an elevated platform while the temporary access barrier had been removed.
The printer in the maintenance office was not working and was reported to the IT support team.
A vehicle reversed toward a work area while a pedestrian was standing behind the vehicle with no clear line of communication with the driver.
A storage cabinet door in the office was found slightly damaged and was scheduled for replacement.
A pressure-containing component was loosened during maintenance before the team confirmed that trapped pressure had been fully released.
Several workers reported that the drinking-water dispenser in the rest area needed servicing.
A worker noticed an unusual smell near a process area, but the fixed gas detection system was unavailable for maintenance.
The paint on a safety sign at the facility entrance had faded and the sign was scheduled for repainting.
A crane was moving a heavy load when the designated lifting signal was lost and personnel remained within the potential movement area.
A computer monitor in the planning office was positioned too low and an employee reported mild neck discomfort.
